text:
'Name' in 'name-and-form' is a formal name. It is an apparent name.
  'Form' in 'name-and-form' is a nominal form. It is a form only in
  name.

say: 'Name' in 'name-and-form' is a formal name. It is an apparent name. 'Form' in 'name-and-form' is a nominal form. It is a form only in name.

text:
It is as if one is trying to outstrip one's shadow by running towards
it out of fun, while the other is trying to flee from it out of fear.

say: It is as if one is trying to outstrip one's shadow by running towards it out of fun, while the other is trying to flee from it out of fear.

text: Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. Because of contact, feeling. What one feels, one perceives. What one perceives, one reasons about. What one reasons about, one turns into papañca. What one turns into papañca, owing to that papañcasaññāsankhā beset him.
The comparison of this discourse to a honey-ball is understandable, since it holds the secret of the latent tendencies towards dogmatic views.
Just as if a man overcome by hunger came upon a honey-ball.
When vitakka breaks loose and runs riot, it creates a certain deluded state of mind, which is papanca.

say: Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is where senses hit the world. Because of where senses hit the world, pleasant-or-unpleasant tone. What one feels, one perceives. What one perceives, one reasons about. What one reasons about, one turns into papanca. What one turns into papanca, owing to that papancasannasankha — spiralling stories out of everything, perceiving and counting and naming — beset him.. The comparison of this discourse to a honey-ball is understandable, since it holds the secret of the latent tendencies towards dogmatic views.. Just as if a man overcome by hunger came upon a honey-ball.. When vitakka breaks loose and runs riot, it creates a certain deluded state of mind, which is papanca.
spiralling

text:
Gods and men delight in existence, they are attached to existence...
When Dhamma is being preached to them for the cessation of existence,
their minds do not reach out towards it.

say: Gods and men liking that grabs in existence, they are attached to existence... When Dhamma is being preached to them for the stopping of existence, their minds do not reach out towards it.

text:
From whatever source papañcasaññāsankhā beset a man, if, in regard to
that, there is nothing to be delighted in, asserted, or clung to, then
this itself is the end of the underlying tendencies to attachment, to
aversion, to views, to doubts, to conceit, to attachment towards
existence, and to ignorance.

say: From whatever source papancasannasankha — spiralling stories out of everything, perceiving and counting and naming — beset a man, if, in regard to that, there is nothing to be delighted in, asserted, or clung to, then this itself is the end of the underlying tendencies to attachment, to aversion, to views, to doubts, to conceit, to attachment towards existence, and to not seeing how it works.

text:
The idea behind this occurrence of tides of imaginings is quite often
represented by the concept of asava, influx.

say: The idea behind this occurrence of tides of imaginings is quite often represented by the concept of asava, influx.

text: Steadied whereon the tides of imaginings no longer occur in him.

say: Steadied whereon the tides of imaginings no longer occur in him.

text: He does not delight in Nibbana. Why so? Because he knows that delighting is the root of suffering, and from becoming comes birth and to the one become there is decay-and-death.

say: He does not liking that grabs in Nibbana — out, like a flame with no fuel. Why so? Because he knows that delighting is the root of suffering, and from the next me forming comes birth and to the one become there is decay-and-death.

text: He understands it to be impermanent, uninvolved, unrejoiced.

say: He understands it to be impermanent, uninvolved, unrejoiced.

text:
The nature of consciousness in general is to abide or dwell in. That
nonmanifestative consciousness, however, has got rid of the tendency to
abide or dwell in.

say: The nature of consciousness in general is to abide or dwell in. That nonmanifestative consciousness, however, has got rid of the tendency to abide or dwell in.

text:
There is a certain deep significance in the word yathabhuta. In
contradistinction to the two words bhava and vibhava, the word bhuta
has some peculiarity of its own.

say: There is a certain deep significance in the word yathabhuta — seeing things as they are. In contradistinction to the two words bhava — the next me forming — and vibhava, the word bhuta has some peculiarity of its own.
thirst

text:
The discrimination between an 'internal' and an 'external' is the
outcome of the inability to penetrate name-and-form, to see through it.
There is an apparent duality: I, as one who sees, and name-and-form, as
the objects seen. Between them there is a dichotomy as internal and
external. It is on this very dichotomy that the six sense-bases are
'based'.

say: The discrimination between an 'internal' and an 'external' is the outcome of the inability to penetrate name-and-form, to see through it. There is an apparent duality — I, as one who sees, and name-and-form, as the objects seen. Between them there is a dichotomy as internal and external. It is on this very dichotomy that the six sense-bases are 'based'.

text:
Worldings in general are in the habit of asserting dogmatically 'I
know, I see, it is verily so', jānāmi passāmi tath' eva etaṃ, when
they have a special knowledge or understanding of something or other.

say: Worldings in general are in the habit of asserting dogmatically 'I know, I see, it is verily so', janami passami tath' eva etam, when they have a special knowledge or understanding of something or other.
